one_star_reviews.text:
These guys unfortunately run an unethical business.

Details: I went to pick up my girlfriends car from Action Motor Industries after someone ran into the back of her. There was minimal damage, I just needed to change the tyre over. It was towed (organized by VicRoads) 6kms from Sunshine/Mcintyre Rd by Action Towing to Action Motor Industries at around 5:30pm. Her car was sitting in the front unlocked section overnight and I picked it up about 10:00am the next day. My girlfriend was told it would be $360 or so from the tower which is as per the standard after hours towing costs from an accident. No issue.

Pick up/Cost: The Owner (I assume) starts with telling me it's $950 to get the car back (clearly that is a try on). I ask to see the breakdown of these costs and he says you need to pay first and then you see the breakdown of costs. We argue. His explanations for additional costs were nonsense but he has no shame and he holds the keys. It's not a fair negotiation. I got it down to $600, but still, it's no way to run a business. Obviously avoid this place at all cost and VicRoads needs to weed out businesses like this from their accredited list. They let me borrow a floor jack to change the tyre though.

My partner visited the salon three separate times today to check availability. We completely understand that walk-ins can be difficult to accommodate and that appointments may be required. However, the way the service was refused was completely unacceptable.
As returning customers, we expected to be treated with basic courtesy and professionalism. Instead, the attitude we encountered was unfriendly, dismissive, rude, and highly unprofessional. There is a significant difference between politely explaining that there is no availability and making a customer feel unwelcome or inconvenienced for simply asking.

What is even more disappointing is seeing management actively respond to positive feedback while seemingly avoiding any acknowledgment of legitimate concerns regarding staff conduct. Good customer service is not just about responding to compliments—it is also about taking responsibility when customers have a negative experience.

If management genuinely values its customers, I strongly suggest investing in customer service and professional communication training for staff. The way customers are spoken to and treated reflects directly on the business and its management.

For the prices being charged, the level of customer service should be considerably better. Unfortunately, based on our experience today, I cannot recommend this salon and would strongly encourage others to consider their customer service standards before spending their money here.

I had a very disappointing experience with migration lawyer Ravi and the service provided through his practice.

My initial consultation and migration advice were with Ravi. During the consultation, I was told that I could contact the team if I had further questions or needed clarification regarding the same matter. However, when I later followed up about the same query, even within the same week, I was asked to pay another consultation fee. I found this frustrating and inconsistent with what had originally been communicated.

Toward the end, most of my communication was with Gurpreet, Ravi’s assistant, and unfortunately my experience with her was particularly poor. I found her manner of communication unnecessarily loud and unprofessional. I also felt there was too much pressure around getting students to proceed with admissions and purchase courses, rather than simply providing clear and professional guidance.

Overall, I was disappointed with the level of professionalism, communication, transparency around follow-up fees, and customer service. Based on my personal experience, I would not recommend this migration practice.

Buying was definitely a unique experience:

Ordered a part I needed pretty urgently for an upcoming ride, which was listed on the website as in stock, and in store on the website.

Realised a week later it hadn’t been sent.
Tried to call the shop, rung out, no answer.
Jumped on the website chat, said I was getting transferred to a team member then zero response. Absolutely unacceptable experience.

My daughter was accepted into the Social Savvy program specifically because she struggles with social interaction, emotional regulation and boundaries. Yet only three hours into the program, I was called to remove her because she displayed the EXACT behaviours she was there to receive support with.

What makes this particularly concerning is that these services are supposed to be delivered by highly trained professionals experienced in behaviour and supporting children with additional needs. Yet when my daughter actually became dysregulated and required that expertise, they could not manage or support her participation — they called her mother to take her home.

I was then told she needs intensive one-on-one behaviour therapy. If this program was not equipped to manage her known needs, she should NEVER have been accepted in the first place.

Based on our experience, this program appears far better suited to children who are already well behaved, compliant and easy to manage. It left me seriously questioning what families and the NDIS are actually paying for if children requiring genuine behavioural support become “too difficult” the moment their needs present.

NDIS-funded services should provide meaningful, skilled support — not simply accept participants who are easiest to manage and easiest to bill for.

What made the situation worse was Suzanne’s manner when I collected my daughter. I found her extremely rude, dismissive and lacking in compassion. I felt I was being escorted out rather than treated with basic respect as a parent.

If you cannot manage challenging behaviour, BE TRANSPARENT ABOUT THAT BEFORE ACCEPTING CHILDREN AND THEIR NDIS FUNDING.

Children with additional needs deserve genuine skilled support — not inclusion only while they are convenient and easy to manage.

They will try to say we don't know her behaviourally because they wanted me to sign up with them, absolutely no way after this! Go somewhere else! It's just a business for easy billing.

Very unsatisfactory experience from start to finish. Reception/admin staff in particular very unwelcoming and blunt. Phone line never works, whether this is intentional or not I have no way of knowing. This happens in the same voice, at the same pace and timing every time without fail.

The actual service itself with the Dr was very brief and I wasn’t given much time to discuss my condition of rheumatoid arthritis. No mention of lifestyle, diet, exercise or stress which are all contributing factors to inflammatory conditions. Just immediately put on medication without any consideration. Since my last appointment I have come off the medication, focussed on diet and lifestyle and have seen significant improvement. Will not be continuing my appointments with this service and would not recommend them to anyone else with the same condition.

one_star_reviews.text:
I cannot express to you enough that you shouldn’t go here, part of me would love to describe it as a scam but honestly, it’s just poor care.
Don’t get me wrong, the people are lovely but unfortunately, being lovely people doesn’t actually lead to a successful business being run. They forward book every clients appointments by about 3 sessions, smart at first, but if anything disrupts that, even stuff that isn’t in your control, then it can be weeks before you get another appointment.
This year, I’ve made every effort to go and see a therapist once ~2 weeks, yet because of their stupid booking system, I think it’s currently August and I’m on like session 8.
I’ve been there for over a year because I believe in giving something it’s fair go, but honestly, this place has done nothing but stress me out further and make my life marginally worse through the faff. Maybe you’ll have a lot more luck than I did, and I genuinely hope that you do, I know that trying to find a psychologist that works is awful nowadays, but I urge you to try and find a better place before here, I almost guarantee that you’ll be better in the long run.
Again, as stated, lovely people, but I just don’t think that’s enough, I’d rather they be bad people that operated a functioning service.

one_star_reviews.text:
Absolutely horrified by the quality of these nails. My cousin paid $150 for this set, and seeing what she asked for compared to what she actually received is honestly disgusting.
I am qualified in nails myself, so I know what proper application and finishing should look like, and there are so many issues with this set. The gel polish is flooding into the cuticle area, the edges are uneven, the acrylic looks poorly applied, and the overall shape and finish are nowhere near the standard I would expect from a professional nail service. Even the nail art looks rushed — the dots are inconsistent, the French tips are messy, and the bow detailing barely resembles the reference.
Obviously, a reference photo isn't always going to be replicated perfectly, and that's completely understandable. But this isn't just a case of the design looking a little different. The actual application and technique are what concern me. As someone who is qualified and knows what I'm looking at, this honestly makes me question whether the person who did this set is properly qualified or trained to be charging clients for this standard of work.
$150 for this is absolutely ridiculous. I've personally been to plenty of other nail places, paid significantly less, and received much cleaner and more professional-looking work. For $150, you absolutely should not be leaving with product flooding the cuticle area and such an unfinished, messy result.
I was genuinely shocked when my cousin showed me these. She deserved so much better for what she paid, and as someone with knowledge of nail application, I find this standard of work disgusting. I would not recommend this place based on the set she received.

Went to Moi Clinic as they offered me an NDIS funded initial ASD assessment for my 2.5y.o. Non verbal boy.
The initial appointment involved 1 appointment for parents and 1 for my sister n alone for 30 mins.
We also took on board NDIS funded weekly speech therapy.
At the time of the ASD assessment my boy had approx 3-5 words.
It took 6 months to receive the results.
During those 6 months we had weekly speech therapy and daily speech work/therapy by parents.
After all that hard work we managed to add an additional 3-5 words.
Because the assessment results took so long we opted to go to a psychiatrist as we were already on a wait list and had arrived to the top of that list.
After multiple appointments and a DNA test the psychiatrist indicated that he met the criteria and we would be getting a diagnosis.
Then the results from Moi came thru and we were absolutely baffled by the outcome.
Moi clinics results were basically as follows: ‘your son has ASD characteristics/traits but due to his ability to add as few more words he does not meet the dsm criteria yet. We recommend further speech therapy and a re- assessment in a couple/few years.
So they took over $2000 of NDIS money for our son to tell us that he has ASD traits but is too young to diagnose yet as he has learned a couple more words.
There are multiple issues with this. 1st) there telling us something we already know and it didn’t need $2000 to tell us he has ASD traits.
2nd) they failed to look at the evidence of a failed brigance test and the fact that a 3 y.o can only say 5-10 words and does not communicate with us.
3rd) that there results are not in harmony with a more qualified and older Psychiatrist who has dealt with more ASD in his lifetime then they have.
When I tried to explain this it was met with offence.
If you want real help for your children best avoid moi clinic.

one_star_reviews.text:
ACU: A Complete Disaster — Think Twice Before Enrolling

I previously studied a Bachelor of Business online at La Trobe University and was very happy with my experience. I decided to pursue a Bachelor of Commerce at ACU because it offered online study and direct enrolment without going through a tertiary admissions centre. I thought a commerce degree would open up more job opportunities. Unfortunately, my experience at ACU has been extremely disappointing, and I regret my decision.

From outdated course notes and textbooks to poorly organised units, the quality of teaching and student support has been far below my expectations. Some lecturers rely heavily on scripts rather than explaining concepts clearly, and I have struggled with the English communication and delivery of some online lectures. In one recorded lecture, I noticed ChatGPT and Google Gemini open on the lecturer’s screen while he was presenting course notes. This raised concerns about the possible use of AI in preparing lectures and assessing students’ work.

Examination arrangements have also been frustrating. I experienced technical problems during an online exam and was subsequently given a deferred exam with a different case study, putting me at a disadvantage compared with students who sat the original exam. In another exam, a Proctorio calculator was listed as available but was not provided, forcing me to perform calculations manually under timed conditions.

What made matters worse was the lack of communication. I repeatedly waited weeks for updates from lecturers and course coordinators, only to receive messages saying an update would be provided soon. I also felt that my formal complaint was closed without a proper investigation.

Students pay for a university education and deserve well-prepared learning materials, competent teaching, fair examinations and timely communication. Instead, I have spent far too much time chasing staff for answers rather than focusing on my studies.

Having experienced a much better online learning environment at La Trobe University, the contrast has been shocking. I am now considering transferring elsewhere.

My advice to prospective students: think twice before enrolling at ACU, especially if you intend to study online. Do your research before committing your time and money. The convenience of online study means very little if the teaching, communication and student support do not meet reasonable expectations.

I’m very disappointed with how my experience with this clinic and psychologist ultimately ended.

I was seeing my psychologist during an incredibly difficult and traumatic period of my life. Throughout that time, I often carried a general sense of not feeling fully heard or understood, particularly given the circumstances I was going through and how vulnerable I was at the time.

Unfortunately, after experiencing one traumatic loss, I went on to experience another. My psychologist was aware of what I had been through. She then went away on holidays, and afterwards I received no follow-up or contact from her. I was left wondering what had happened and ultimately had to reach out myself to explain how hurt and upset I was.

I did receive an apology and a response, which I appreciated. However, I still felt that I was left without a real explanation for what had happened, and the response didn’t resolve the hurt and disappointment I was feeling about how everything had been handled.

The way the therapeutic relationship ended was particularly painful because it amplified that existing sense of not feeling heard or understood. At a time when I was already dealing with an enormous amount of grief and trauma, this left me feeling incredibly let down and, honestly, even more alone.

I understand that psychologists have holidays, personal lives and circumstances outside of work, and I’m not suggesting that they should be available at all times. However, when someone is seeking professional psychological support during one of the most vulnerable periods of their life, I believe communication, appropriate follow-up and consideration of the client’s circumstances are incredibly important.

The last thing I believe a client should be left feeling is more alone, unheard or unsupported as a result of how their therapeutic relationship is handled. Therapy requires trust, and opening up to someone about deeply personal and traumatic experiences is not easy in the first place. Finding a therapist you feel comfortable with and trust can take a lot of time, and I had been seeing this psychologist for quite some time and had already gone through that process of building a therapeutic relationship.

Now, because that trust has been broken, I have had to start the process all over again and find another therapist. Having to open up from the beginning, build that trust again and explain everything I have been through is incredibly difficult and distressing in itself. It is an additional burden at a time when I was already dealing with more than enough, and it was something I really did not need to have to deal with on top of everything else.

Ultimately, this experience has left me feeling hurt, disappointed and very let down. I’m sharing this because the way a therapeutic relationship ends matters, particularly when someone is already in an extremely vulnerable position. I really hope that my experience highlights how much communication, compassion and appropriate follow-up can matter to a client who is going through an incredibly difficult time.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am recording this here because what happened should be part of the public record of this business.

The night before our appointment, I explained that my mother had just been diagnosed with a severe brain tumour, was in hospital, and was facing high-risk brain surgery on Monday. Friday was the last practical opportunity we had to deal with time-sensitive financial and estate matters beforehand.

I was met with sympathy and accommodation and was specifically asked to send through the matters we wanted to discuss in advance.

I did exactly that.

The following morning, my mother obtained gate leave from hospital and we organised our morning around travelling to Woy Woy for the 11:00 AM appointment.

At 9:58 AM, roughly one hour before it was due to begin, Meany & Associates cancelled.

Their explanation was that much of the broader material fell outside the scope of their services and that they did not consider themselves the appropriate practice.

An accounting firm is entitled to decline work. That is not my complaint.

My complaint is the timing and the way a seriously ill woman was handled after an appointment had been arranged, advance material had been requested, and hospital leave and travel had already been organised around it.

At 10:15 AM I asked them to reconsider. I expressly reiterated the brain tumour diagnosis, told them that we had travelled for the appointment, and offered to abandon the broader matters and reduce the appointment primarily to the CGT implications.

At 10:25 AM, Meany & Associates acknowledged the diagnosis, acknowledged that we had travelled, and said they appreciated the urgency of the situation.

They still declined to proceed, even with the reduced scope.

That is what I found callous.

They knew the situation was urgent. They knew a hospital patient and her family had already organised their morning around attending. They were offered a materially reduced scope. They still would not work with us.

I do not suggest that an accountant must accept every client or provide advice outside its competence. I do believe that the way a professional services firm handles commitments, particularly where a seriously ill person has relied on them and time is plainly limited, is highly relevant to prospective clients.

I have retained the relevant emails, call records, appointment details and contemporaneous correspondence.

Meany & Associates is welcome to publicly explain what happened. Prospective clients can read the facts and decide for themselves what this episode says about the firm's judgement, reliability and treatment of people when circumstances become difficult.

My experience of Meany & Associates in Woy Woy was cold, inflexible and, in my opinion, profoundly lacking in basic consideration.

My recommendation is simple: avoid at all costs.

one_star_reviews.text:
I had abdominoplasty with liposuction with Dr Gahankari after weight loss in my 40s, at a cost of over $20k. I’m writing this so other patients can make an informed decision.

At the consultation I was shown a single photo of his previous work, one side-on photo of one patient with a flat stomach and no visible scarring, which set my expectations high. I was told to have “realistic expectations,” but this was not defined in the contract and I don’t recall the specific limitations which he later raised being explained to me at consultation or in the contract. My results were nowhere near what I expected based on the photo I was shown.

In the months after surgery I raised concerns about several areas that were insufficiently treated or unchanged. The explanations I received varied from appointment to appointment: armpit fat was described as excess skin, then later breast tissue and muscle; my love handles were described as bone, though I could push them in; my inner thighs had insufficient fat at one visit and excess skin at the next. I found these explanations inconsistent and confusing, and I was left feeling my concerns weren’t being taken seriously.

I was repeatedly told we’d discuss revision a year after surgery. My recollection is that in-rooms revision was offered at no cost. When the time came, I was told in-rooms anaesthesia was limited and I’d likely need to stop partway through. When I asked about doing it in hospital instead, I was quoted a further fee for his work which I couldn’t afford. When I asked by email why adequate removal of my love handles couldn’t be guaranteed, it took repeated follow-ups to get a reason, and after I questioned his response the correspondence stopped.

I raised this through the formal complaints process, but I’m left largely where I started. My honest opinion is that I would have sought a second opinion if the limitations had been explained clearly at the consultation. I’ve had to buy a new wardrobe to cover the results and I’m embarrassed about how I look.

⭐️ 1 STAR — “2 YEARS AND COUNTING: THE PROGRAMMED RUNAROUND”
If Programmed ACT ever decides to open a customer-service training course, I strongly recommend attending — preferably as a customer, because apparently that's the only way to experience the full masterclass in repetitive bullshit and passing the buck. 😂
We're talking about an 80-year-old ACT Housing tenant who has been waiting approximately TWO YEARS for trees to be dealt with because of their proximity to powerlines.
Two. Years.
At this point, the trees have probably got their own tenancy agreement. 🌳🏠
Every time you follow up, it's like entering the Programmed Customer Service Groundhog Day:
☎️ Call
➡️ Explain the problem
➡️ Explain it again
➡️ Get the same generic response
➡️ Follow up
➡️ Explain it AGAIN
➡️ Repeat indefinitely 🔄
The only thing that seems to be getting maintained is the excuse rotation.
Honestly, the trees have probably had more consistent growth than this job has had progress.
And let's not forget the customer service — because apparently “customer service” means making an elderly tenant repeatedly chase the same issue while everyone involved perfects the ancient art of “that's someone else's problem.”
Two years for a tree-removal issue involving powerlines isn't exactly the definition of “efficient.”
At this rate, the trees will be mature enough to start paying rent before Programmed manages to remove them. 🌳💰
Programmed ACT: where your problem goes in circles so long it eventually becomes a recreational activity.
⭐️ Would I recommend?
Only if you enjoy:
Repeating yourself approximately 47 times
Getting nowhere
Chasing people who apparently have mastered invisibility
And receiving enough repetitive bullshit to fertilise the very trees you're waiting to have removed.
0/10 for customer service.
10/10 for making an elderly tenant wonder if the trees will outlive the complaint.
Maybe next year we'll review the progress.
Oh wait…
We've already been waiting two years. 🤦‍♀️🌳

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely poor service – four weeks to resolve a straightforward dispatch error

Our experience with this company has been extremely disappointing and, quite frankly, unacceptable.

An order was delivered incorrectly, and what should have been a straightforward correction turned into an approximately four-week ordeal involving multiple phone calls, emails and repeated follow-ups from our team.

The biggest issue has been dealing with the warehouse/dispatch side of the business, particularly Wes. Deadlines and promised call-backs were repeatedly not met, meaning we were continually left having to chase the matter ourselves. On more than one occasion, we were told something would be dealt with or followed up, only to find that it had not happened.

What made the situation even more frustrating was the constant changing of the goalposts regarding what needed to be done, who needed to make the next call and what information or action was supposedly required. Instead of taking ownership of the problem and seeing it through to resolution, we were repeatedly required to follow up and push for progress.

This is not a case of an isolated delay. Four weeks, numerous emails and multiple phone calls to correct an order that the company supplied incorrectly is simply not an acceptable level of service.

The amount of time our staff have had to spend chasing this issue has been completely disproportionate to the problem itself. A professional dispatch and warehouse operation should be able to identify an incorrect delivery, communicate clearly, meet its commitments and resolve the issue without the customer having to continually chase it.

Unfortunately, our experience has demonstrated a serious lack of communication, follow-through and accountability. Based on this experience, we would be very reluctant to recommend this company to other businesses that depend on reliable ordering, dispatch and customer service.

They water down the fruit juice, it has almost no flavour. The food is otherwise better than most SRSs, though who serves pasta with grated cheese, and calls it "macaroni cheese"?

They do almost no maintenance here. The ceilings leak. The floor is dangerously uneven. Carpet tiles are coming up. My shower didn't work when I moved in, and it took them 6 months to fix it, despite repeated polite requests to fix it, and despite a medical need for a hot shower. Meanwhile, they charged me for an en suite! I had to walk to the other end of the house and use a communal shower with no curtain or lock on the door.

If I ask for extra help, they'll only actually help about half the time.

When I was sick in hospital recently, they did not secure my room, so hundreds of dollars of my belongings were stolen. I tried to complain to the manager - she seemed bored, did not apologise or offer compensation, and I have had no official response to my complaint. I think this is a serious matter that they ought to be very sorry for, but that's just me, I guess.

The cleaner throws away your belongings, they refuse to apologise and don't offer to replace what has been stolen, she brings a dark energy into the room, and is nosy and rude.

However, they lost most of my tea towels and replaced them quickly when I complained.

They charge your NDIS package an outrageous amount for doing nothing much, while giving the impression at the look around interview that they might take a couple of hundred a fortnight. I have reported this SRS to the NDIS.

This would be a good enough budget SRS if they did not charge ridiculous amounts to your NDIS package. I don't like that I was misled about how much they would take. However, this accommodation certainly is not worth the amount of money they have charged me, and they have yet to respond to my complaints about this matter.

They allow small, well-behaved pets, which is nice. Some of the staff are lovely. The residents are mostly lovely. It's a good location. However, because of the outrageous, ludicrous, charges to your NDIS package, I advise you not to move in here.

When we asked to reschedule because we were going to be overseas, they refused and still charged us the full consultation fee. 2. Responding to your comments as i’m no able to reply:

I genuinely hope you've learned a lesson from this rather than simply taking people's money and ignoring their concerns. Your staff, especially your receptionists, seriously need some customer service training. The way we were spoken to was disgraceful. ( it’s also obvious in older google comments)

It doesn't even deserve 1 star but there was no other option. The food was so terrible my Labrador sniffed it and walked away. My mother rang the bell for assistance to go to  the the bathroom, it either was answered two hours later or not at all. Her drawers were crawling with hundreds of cockroaches, dead and alive. I alerted staff and asked for some pest control substance. They replied they couldn't access any. When my mum came out of hospital and returned to her room at Tricare, she needed to go to the toilet. The Staff left her alone and she blacked out from an horrific fall. They later allowed her to fall from her chair, her skull was pierced by a sharp object. THEY NEVER EXPLAINED WHAT HAPPENED despite numerous requests.She died several days later. Then, they charged an extra 15K for their EXTRA care? They refused to honour the contract UNLESS WE PAID FIFTEEN THOUSAND DOLLARS FOR THE WORST NIGHTMARE OF ANY LIFE. Mum was a dignified person who had dedicated her life to the betterment  of others.Tricare Labrador should be shut down.She wasn't  allowed fruit juice, drinks were the weakest,cheapest cordial. Kitchen staff told me they were forced to serve this unless doctor ordered juice due to constipation. I was told the total allowance per resident for food was $2 per day? The WORST and most telling proof of neglect was massive deep bedsores that we were told were dressed but on inspection were NOT. My mother was in such agony the doctor had to give her morphine patches and Fentanol. I could fill a journal with numerous examples of sustained suffering.The air-conditioned remotes were hidden & the patients sweltered in the oppressive HEAT. The only food Mum ate was what we brought in.The kind staff brought fruit & gave it to Mum, they were so sorry for her. The only RN overseeing the whole place on weekends did not have the requisite standard of English. Complaints were answered with stock phrases, blank expressions, promises that never eventuated. Mostly, we waited at the empty desk and no-one appeared. At least, we were unable to locate them. My many regrets are exacerbated by my failure to send a report to the Parliamentary Enquiry. I didn't have Power of Attorney so had no authority to choose or change the facility.
I read your reply. I am willing to swear in court about what I wrote. I spoke to the kitchen cook MYSELF. She said, unless Mum had bowel trouble diagnosed by the Dr, she was NOT allowed juice, ONLY CORDIAL. There were TWO staff who witnessed the hundreds of dead and alive cockcroaches. THEY were the ones who told me the treatment was upstairs, locked in a cupboard. I can SHOW you where the aircon remotes were kept. NO patient could reach them.My mother HAD BRUISES on her head and body from falls and the final one killed her. I WROTE to TRICARE with PHOTOS of white bread sandwiches with minimal filling. I received AN APOLOGY and a promise to improve. I was employed at a University for fifty years, working with languages. I recognise the ability or otherwise re command of English. Our family could NOT make ourselves understood to the ONLY R.N on duty on weekends.
A close friend is an EXPERIENCED medical specialist. HE EXAMINED AND CONFIRMED the appalling lack of professional care of my Mother's BED SORES. He said that was THE measuring stick. I reported they were raw and exposed. I was told they were treated and covered. THEY WERE NOT. My sister visited every day.. She can no longer even drive or walk past your building such are our HORRIFIC NIGHTMARES.
I just watched Maggie Beer and her wish to improve nutrient standards. That stimulated this second message. Only now, did I see your reply. I have four other witnesses of the below standard aspects of this "residence". One reoved her Mum after only two weeks there, never to return. There is NOT one aspect I cannot prove. I also reported these concerns to my Member of Parliament. The artificial additives & preservatives in the desserts meant even that pleasure was denied.
I couldnt remove Mum as I didnt have Power of Attorney.

I would NEVER recommend them to anyone.

I wonder if the Vantage Strata team are actually going to clean Lift 4 at Manuka Terrace today, or whether the floor will once again get a filthy mop run over it, spreading the grime around before being passed off as “clean”.

At this point, I can only speculate whether the grime embedded in the floor will actually be removed or simply “shined” again and called cleaning. Then there are the walls, with their visible layer of slime, residue and grime seemingly left untouched.

Lift 4 has become a metal tomb of grime and filth. The floor gets its ceremonial “shine”, while the mess on the walls remains.

It is my opinion, this is not an isolated poor clean. It is an ongoing and systemic problem. The quality of cleaning services at Manuka Terrace — particularly in the lifts — is appalling.

When the same plainly visible problems are allowed to persist, this is no longer just about the performance of a cleaning contractor. It is a direct reflection of Vantage Strata's management and oversight of a service it is being paid to manage.

Residents should not have to repeatedly point out that communal areas remain visibly dirty. Nor should a lift look filthy after it has supposedly been cleaned. A basic quality check should identify these issues immediately.

And before the inevitable response inviting me to contact your GM to “discuss my concerns” — don't bother. The concern is already perfectly clear: clean the lift properly and ensure the cleaning contractor is actually delivering the service residents are paying for.

Residents shouldn't need to contact senior management or engage in another round of corporate correspondence to get a lift properly cleaned.

Vantage Strata is being paid to manage these services. Manage them.

Check the work. Hold the contractor accountable. Use clean equipment. Remove the grime from the floor. Clean the residue from the walls. Stop accepting a standard that anyone walking into Lift 4 can plainly see is inadequate.

This isn't about another discussion. It's about delivering the service residents are already paying for. Less damage control. More quality control. Clean the lift properly.

It’s been 3 months since I had my consult with Sarah and after suffering with repeated clogged ducts, mastitis and feeding issues I have come back to reflect on my experience with The Milky Days and provide some honest feedback.

Unfortunately, I feel very disappointed and let down by the service I received from Sarah. After booking an initial consult 3 weeks after my son was born, Sarah helped me by addressing my concerns about a milk oversupply and put forward a plan in place. This was a great help, I was told to check in via email in a couple of days to reevaluate how things were going and put forward a new plan from there. This happened. Sarah suggested in this correspondence that we review again in a couple of days to see how things were going. I followed that advice and checked in, but received no response. 3 days later I sent a follow up email asking Sarah whether she received my email, and again received no response. After this I did not reach out again and never received a response from Sarah. It has now been 3 almost 4 months.

As a paying customer, I feel I was charged $250 to basically be told to block feed for a couple of days and then left in the dark with no answer on how to feed moving forward in the future, and left as a first time mum to guess and fill in the gaps myself. If further communication and reviews needed another consult to be booked, I would have understood this. However, I’m unsure why I wasn’t informed or responded to? Very disappointing to essentially be ghosted by a professional I put my trust in during such a vulnerable time. It was especially disappointing to be waiting for a response whilst seeing posts constantly flowing on her social media page.

Based on my honest experience, I would not recommended The Milky Days to mums on the Sunshine Coast.

I had my rhinoplasty with this doctor, and unfortunately, my overall experience has been extremely disappointing.

At my initial consultation, I was told that my nose may actually be too small and that I may need filler. This was nowhere close to what ended up happening. After my surgery, I was left with concerns about the appearance and straightness of my nose, which I raised with the doctor.

During a consultation, the doctor confirmed that my nose was not straight and said, word for word, that he “doesn’t know what to say” and had “no words for me.” He then said that my nose not being straight was my face’s fault and continued pointing out other features of my face.

At one point, while I was crying, he pulled out a ruler and began measuring the distance between my eyes from a SCREEN a photo of me from when I was 18.I found this extremely upsetting, particularly at a time when I was already visibly distressed and trying to discuss my concerns about my nose.

As a patient who trusted a surgeon with such a significant procedure, I expected my concerns to be listened to and addressed with understanding and professionalism. Instead, I left feeling blamed for the outcome and extremely uncomfortable with the way the consultation was handled.

I’m sharing my experience because I believe people considering rhinoplasty should be able to make an informed decision and understand that the experience can extend well beyond the surgery itself.

one_star_reviews.text: Don't even think about it....... Theses people are BAD

Dont let your loved one end up here. My mother in law spent 18 months in this place. 90 residents 1 cleaner, no maintenace person. The place is filthy and faliing apart. My mother in law had a small bed sore on her heel 6 months ago. My wife over that time asked how it was when she visited every 2nd day as they had it permanently covered with a medical boot. 1 week before she passed away we got a call from Gold Coast hospital saying that she had been admitted with a terrible infection on her heel and it was full of maggots. Her foot needed to be amputated but as the infection had been neglected for so long it had traveled through her blood, bones and her organs had begun to shut down. She was not going to survive the surgery. Alex the manager told us the the wound care team had instructed the staff to check and dress it every 3 days. The gangrene that had set had been developing  for at least 3 months according to doctors at the hospital. Shows the care level and neglect this place offers. Mum passed away 2 days after arriving to hospital. Mum was also diabetic and it must have been a chore to give insulin each day so they took her off insulin and told.  my wife that her sugar levels were good now. Her death certificate said her cause of death was due to infection and diabetes. Stay away from here. The aged care commission is investigating.

Hi my name is Silvia. My beautiful Mum was in Tricare Pimpama for around 18 months. After the first 3 months I approached Head office to question why the place was so dirty. I was told the place was just old. I said it may be old but it didn't have to be dirty. A few things got done but not near my satisfaction, therefore I ended up cleaning the walls myself in my mums room. I requested the divider curtain to be washed many times before it got done. I asked for the toilet seat be repaired as it was attached with only 1 hinge and was dangerous and was shared by 3 other residents. As nothing was done I asked some of the staff what was going on. They advised me there was a list pages long of maintenance jobs to be completed but did not have a maintenance person. These tasks were to be attended by the cleaning lady. After 6 months mum was screaming out in pain for 2 days so they finally called an ambulance and took her to Robina hospital. They informed us that mum had a bad UTI. Her urine had turned to puss.
5 months later the staff told be that mum had a bed sore on her left heel and was to wear a medical boot at all times. I frequently asked how the bed sore was going a was told there is nothing to worry about. Mum had been a diabetic for 10 years so I asked them why mum had been taken off insulin. I was told her glucose levels were good and she didn't need it any more.
4 weeks ago mum was admitted to Gold Coast uni Hospital. The doctors called us and told us mum's left heel was full of maggots and gangrene had set in some time ago. Her foot needed to be amputated but because the infection had travelled through her blood, bones and organs, she would only live for a few more days anyway. 3 days later she passed away. Our family is extremely upset that this beautiful caring and loving lady had her life cut short by neglect. Even carers told myself they had advised nursing staff that the wound needed attention as it didn't look good. We sincerely hope that nobody else's loved one need to go through these circumstances of neglect. It is also disappointing that no management staff have contacted us offering condolences or apologise for their neglect. All residents need to be shown care and respect .

My mother was a resident there she was neglected. She had a UTI. They drunk her when she was crying out in pain. She had a bad sore on her heel which was neglected until when she went to hospital it was full of maggots and the beginning of gangrene unfortunately that was what killed my mother. She ended up dying of sepsis due to lack of care. Don’t ever send any family member to TRICARE.

I'm honestly not so sure why these people are rated so highly - possibly because they are cheap?
The service they provide is disturbing for a so called business. It is clear they do not care about the customer and make their money from volume sales, which is all they seem to care about!
I sent two query on their website which were apparently not received and then I reached out via their instavram page, mentioning I had some questions prior to making a booking. The response i received was very vaige (English clearly not their first language) and then a link to book after stating they had not received my messages. I then went ahead and asked the questions i had which was simply about how long do they spend with you, as the website says both 30mins and also 15 for $33 (which mind you, if its 15minutes for $33, this is actually not a good deal - especially in a group setting). I also asked about health insurance benefits and pregnancy. This is the response I received:
"Hi we are not suited to your needs. Better to go with the other places. All the best" and then they blocked me!
I had been referred here to my midwife (which now will be telling her the story and to get her to stop referring people here). Disgusting service and im so glad I dodged a bullet by wasting my money here.
If you are after a therapist who actually cares, knows what they are doing, answers all questions and sits with you one on one, I'd recommend going to Health Spot in Randwick. They seem to cost more, but their services for acupuncture are $140ish for an entire hour and you can also claim through healthcare benefits.
I really do hope this post has helped individuals who are looking for quality professionals that actually care, rather than an in and out money making scheme.

Do not use this business.
They prey on the vulnerable.
I was referred to Calm space through my GP on a mental health care plan.
Calm Space were very quick to lock in an appointment and very thorough with explaining their process so they can take your money.
I was told that there would be no Medicare rebate even though I was told differently by my GP.
This didn’t register with me at the time as I was not in a good mental state at the time of making the appointment.
I called the next day to question about the Medicare rebate and was told they could rebook with a different Psychologist but they would charge me an extra fee which happens to be the same amount as the Medicare rebate.
I could not believe what I was hearing.
By this time if I canceled my appointment I had to pay for my appointment anyway.
I canceled anyway as how could I go to someone for help when they are fraudulent and only care about ripping people off instead of actually helping them.

Hubby got two cakes, carrot and chocolate and all I can say they were very dry emphasise dry. They were that dry they induced choking. Plus the chicken kebab was way past its prime also. These kinds of food only keep their freshness for so long. Next time bin them don’t sell them.

one_star_reviews.text:
When someone passes away, there is rarely clarity or experience at play for the people suddenly responsible for what happens next.

For me, this was my first time calling a funeral home to organise someone to take care of a “body”. The man who had passed away was my friend and colleague, and I was supporting his wife, who is also my friend and colleague, through an incredibly difficult time. I found myself standing alone in a hospital hallway, completely outside my comfort zone, trying to work out what I was supposed to do. I called the first name on the list I was given: Darwin Funeral Services.

**My first mistake.**

As soon as I gave Brendan my friend’s name and home community, it was clear he understood he was dealing with an Aboriginal family. During that first conversation, he told me not to bring the children when the family came in to make arrangements because **“Aboriginal kids throw stones.”**

That was the moment I should have hung up.

For the record, the children he was making assumptions about are better behaved than my own balanda children. The assumption was offensive and completely unnecessary.

When I later brought my friend’s wife, mother and grandmother in to complete paperwork and choose a coffin, I had written his name on a piece of paper specifically so it did not need to be spoken aloud. This cultural consideration was seemingly not understood, and despite my efforts to avoid his name being repeatedly spoken, it continued throughout the conversation. In a place like Darwin, I would have thought this was relatively common knowledge within the funeral industry, particularly for someone with many years of experience working with families across the Top End. The lack of awareness was incredibly disappointing.

There were numerous other moments that demonstrated a lack of cultural understanding. On one occasion I phoned simply to ask about the progress of the coffin. The first response was **“Have they paid?”** — despite the family having paid a considerable time earlier. Given the assumptions already made about this family, that comment sat particularly poorly with me.

The coffin itself was also considerably delayed, with sick leave and jury duty given as explanations. I appreciate that unexpected things happen, but when a grieving family is waiting to take their loved one home, I did not find those delays acceptable. Given everything I had experienced by that point, I couldn't help wondering whether a non-Indigenous family would have received the same level of urgency.

There were positives, and it is only fair that I acknowledge them. The flowers used were good quality, and the assistance provided with NLC and PATS paperwork was genuinely helpful.

Even payment, however, was unnecessarily difficult — there was no EFTPOS facility, which I found extraordinary in 2026.

I imagine this review may be water off a duck’s back. Perhaps Darwin Funeral Services provides a perfectly acceptable service to many Darwin families. I can only speak to what I personally witnessed and experienced.

In my experience, Brendan and Darwin Funeral Services were **not culturally safe**.

If writing this saves even one grieving family from experiencing additional distress at an already devastating time, then I am happy to have written it.

Would I use their services again? **Absolutely not.**

My experience with my psychologist has been okay. However, the phone service genuinely ruined my experience with Headspace and I cannot stress this enough.

I've been seeing Headspace ever since February up until early August, so I've been with Headspace Liverpool for around 6 months. Every single time I have done this, I have never received a text or call back. It seems nobody is ever able to get to the phone at Headspace and I am always sent to this prompt. As I have been unable to reschedule another appointment thanks to their horrible phone service, my case with Headspace was closed without my permission, despite me constantly reaching out and calling Headspace to reschedule. I have tried to call multiple times and was sent to this system every time.

I thought my mental health was getting better, but I have been cut off from Headspace and my calls were never answered. Fix your poor phone service before advertising yourself as a mental health service, because instead of helping that only made me more stressed.

I first called about 2–3 weeks ago. I was told the person who conducted my son’s initial session was on holiday. I specifically requested a call back and never received one.

Today, I called at 9:05 a.m., 9:12 a.m., 12:33 p.m., and 12:46 p.m. No one answered, and I have not received a return call despite leaving a message.

Can you please explain how we are supposed to access the help we need when calls are not answered and messages are not returned?

one_star_reviews.text:
After recently having moved to the area, I popped into this salon on a random afternoon with a reference photo. I was not yet set on changing my usual salon and wanted to gauge pricing. I was told to return to the salon on a day where a more senior stylist would be present for a “second opinion”. So I locked in a time and returned.

My chat with the more ‘senior stylist’ (aka the salon Director) lasted around 20 minutes (maybe less). I was effectively advised I would not be able to achieve my reference photo and to explore other solutions. Then, I was told this conversation was going to cost me $80.

I was shocked.

When I questioned why I had not been advised of the ‘consult fee’ at any earlier stage, the Director replied (in an entirely condescending manner) “everything costs money these days hun”. When I refuted the payment, the Director suggested security footage would have to be reviewed. This felt like an accusation of dishonesty or theft on my part which was entirely not the case. She told me the $80 ‘consult fee’ was imposed because I could take her advice and explore cheaper options elsewhere. She told me that in the time that she took to explain to me my reference photo was unachievable, she could have been monetising her time with real appointments (notwithstanding the salon was not full at the time). She told me I was essentially cheating a small business.

Eventually, I was “let go”.

I would like to make it abundantly clear that I was at no time prior to my conversation told that I was sitting through a “consultation”, or that the “consultation” would cost me $80. As it turns out, the Cole & Co website does not even offer a “consult” as a service that can be booked. As far as I know, the fee imposed on me was entirely fiction.

This experience and the implication that I was stealing from the business made me feel distressed. I walked in with good intentions of supporting the business given its within close proximity to my home.

Really poor customer service from the salon Director. Please be warned that the salon is not transparent with pricing at all. The condescending and accusatory nature of the director is especially the reason why I will not be returning in the future.

For $170 for 50 minutes, expect and demand so  much more.

one_star_reviews.text:
I had an extremely disappointing experience with this salon from beginning to end.

My original appointment was for 12pm for a relaxer, for which I had already paid a $127 deposit. I called the day before to advise that I had changed my mind and instead wanted simple cornrows, priced at $79. The salon confirmed this was fine. Given the significant price difference, I would have expected the excess payment to be addressed automatically, or at the very least for a refund to have been initiated and communicated to me.

I arrived at approximately 12:10pm. There was no greeting, no hello and barely any acknowledgement beyond being told to take a seat. Despite having an appointment, I was then left waiting for around 35–40 minutes before my hair was started.

After completing approximately three cornrows, the stylist told me she would be back shortly and disappeared for another 10–15 minutes. When I later got up to use the bathroom, I walked past the office and saw her sitting inside on her phone.

Unfortunately, after all of that, the quality of the cornrows themselves wasn’t even good. They were visibly crooked, unevenly spaced and poorly measured. These were simple straight-back cornrows. I specifically booked and paid a professional salon because I expected a professional result. If I wanted imperfect, crooked cornrows that looked like I’d attempted them myself, I could have stayed home and done exactly that for free.

At the end of the appointment, I specifically asked about the refund for the difference between the $127 I had paid and the $79 service I actually received. I was told that the admin team had been messaged and that they would let me know. By the end of the day, I still had no confirmation that my refund had even been processed.

Basic customer service and basic professionalism were missing throughout the entire experience. At the absolute minimum, greet your clients, communicate delays, complete the service without unnecessary interruptions, provide work to a professional standard, and promptly return money owed.

Abysmal experience. I would not return.
